source.note: supportWindows transcribed from content/docs/2.21/operate/cluster.md 'Kubernetes Compatibility' at the pinned ref — the table the vendor publishes for EVERY KEDA line (one page, newest docs version; the same table appears under content/docs/<v>/ for older versions and the 2.21 copy is the superset). KEDA calls this window TESTED, not supported: 'The tested window of Kubernetes versions with KEDA follows an N-2 approach ... maintainers can decide to extend this ... but there is no guarantee'. There is no separate 'supported' column to prefer (cert-manager has one; KEDA does not), so the tested matrix is the hop source and every surface that renders it must say 'tested'. KEDA is community-supported (governance SUPPORT.md: 'at least' N-2, no guarantee) and publishes NO per-line end-of-life dates, so no row carries eol and no VENDOR_EOL hop exists for KEDA; a line that the matrix lists but upstream no longer patches is not told apart. Floor is 2.7 (the oldest row in the table); 2.8 and 2.7 share the 1.17-1.25 window verbatim. The 2.14 and 2.13 rows share 1.27-1.29 verbatim — transcribed as published, never 'fixed'. Anything older than 2.7 reports VERSION_NOT_IN_CATALOG. NEVER derive a window from go.mod (k8s.io/api v0.36.x at v2.21.0 says nothing about what the operator was tested against). upgradeNotes and rules are EMPTY BY DESIGN: KEDA's breaking changes and deprecations live in the generated-rule pipeline (kb/keda -> k8s-rules/keda), extracted from FIVE upstream paths at pinned tags — CHANGELOG.md (<= v2.20.2; retired at v2.21.0), the GitHub Release body (>= v2.21.0, snapshot committed under kb/keda/upstream/), keda-docs content/docs/<v>/migration.md, the Go struct-tag deprecation ledger (keda:"...deprecated=|deprecatedAnnounce=" diffed tag by tag) and the trigger-type/admission-webhook deltas between adjacent tags. The kedacore/charts repo (chart values such as operator.serviceAccountTokens.mode) is NOT a KB source yet (parked 2026-10-27): chart-value changes ship as hinted platform rules on the keda-operator Deployment.

source.note: Generated by scripts/readiness-agent/extract-github-advisories.py — do not hand-edit. Advisories published on or after 2024-01-01, one bulletin each. Affected = from <= version < fixedIn on the line; fixedIn = the advisory's patched version on that line, never inferred; fixedIn null = the advisory covers every release of the line from `from` on and names no patch there (upgrade to a newer minor). cvssSource: v3 | v4 | legacy | severity (a band's lower bound, not a score).

advisories.title: Privilege escalation from namespace admin to cluster admin via KEDA TriggerAuthentication

bulletins.override: The patched-versions field is blank. KEDA v2.21.0 (released 2026-09-23, the advisory's publication day) ships the fix ('Security: enforce explicit service-account token audiences', the first breaking change in its release notes), so the patch is 2.21.0 and every earlier release on the 2.20 line stays affected (no 2.20.3 was cut).

advisories.title: PostgreSQL connection string parameter injection via incomplete whitespace escaping

bulletins.override: The affected range is written '<= 2.19.x' and the patch as the bare line '2.20': KEDA v2.20.0 (released 2026-06-01, the advisory's publication day) carries the PostgreSQL connection-string fix, so read as every release before 2.20.0, patched in 2.20.0.

advisories.title: Arbitrary File Read via Insufficient Path Validation in HashiCorp Vault Service Account Credential

bulletins.override: Two component rows. Operator: '<=2.17.2,<=2.18.2' is one range (every release up to 2.18.2) with patches on the two maintained lines, 2.17.3 and 2.18.3; '>=2.19.0' is not a patch of an affected line (2.19.0 shipped on 2026-01-?? after the advisory and carries the fix by construction), so it is dropped. Metrics server: the Vault credential file read reached the metrics server only before 2.9.0, when scaler construction moved into the operator; patched 2.9.0.
